options.label: Day first, month in words
options.rule: Write dates with the day first in numerals, the month in words, and the year in numerals. Examples: 6 april 2009; 15 september 2024; 1 november 1990.

options.label: DD-MM-YYYY
options.rule: Write dates in numeric form as DD-MM-YYYY, using leading zeros for single-digit days and months. Examples: 06-04-2009; 15-09-2024; 01-11-1990.

options.label: DD/MM/YYYY
options.rule: Write dates in numeric form as DD/MM/YYYY, using leading zeros for single-digit days and months. Examples: 06/04/2009; 15/09/2024; 01/11/1990.

options.label: DD-MM-YYYY with periods
options.rule: Write dates in numeric form as DD.MM.YYYY, using leading zeros for single-digit days and months. Examples: 06.04.2009; 15.09.2024; 01.11.1990.

options.label: Write years in full
options.rule: Write years in full. Examples: 1989; 2025.

options.label: Abbreviate years with an apostrophe
options.rule: When an abbreviated year is acceptable, write only the last two digits and precede them with an apostrophe. Examples: '89; '25.

options.label: 24-hour clock with colon
options.rule: Use the 24-hour clock with a colon as separator. Examples: 08:30; 17:00; 22:15.

options.label: 24-hour clock with uur
options.rule: Use the 24-hour clock with a period as separator and add the word “uur”. Examples: 08.30 uur; 17.00 uur; 22.15 uur.

options.label: Write times in words
options.rule: When the context is informal or idiomatic, write times in words using standard Dutch expressions. Examples: halfnegen; kwart over drie; tien voor halfzes.

options.label: Use the symbol before the amount, without a space
options.rule: Write currency amounts with the currency symbol before the amount, without a space. Examples: €5; $10.

options.label: Use the symbol before the amount, with a space
options.rule: Write currency amounts with the currency symbol before the amount, with a space. Examples: € 5; $ 10.

options.label: Use the ISO code before the amount
options.rule: Write currency amounts with the ISO currency code before the amount, separated by a space. Examples: EUR 5; USD 10.

options.label: Write the currency name after the amount
options.rule: Write the amount first and the currency name after it. Examples: 5 euro; 10 dollar.

options.label: Use a decimal comma and periods for thousands
options.rule: Use a comma as the decimal separator and periods as thousands separators. Examples: 5,90; 1.250; 15.870,33.

options.label: Use a decimal comma and spaces for thousands
options.rule: Use a comma as the decimal separator and spaces as thousands separators. Examples: 5,90; 1 250; 15 870,33.

options.label: Use a decimal period and commas for thousands
options.rule: Use a period as the decimal separator and commas as thousands separators. Examples: 5.90; 1,250; 15,870.33.

options.label: Use % without a space
options.rule: Write percentages with the percent sign directly after the number, without a space. Example: 99%.

options.label: Use % with a space
options.rule: Write percentages with a space between the number and the percent sign. Example: 99 %.

options.label: Write procent in words
options.rule: Write percentages with the word “procent”. Examples: 99 procent; tien procent.

options.label: Abbreviate with numerals, spell out without
options.rule: Abbreviate units when used with numerals, but spell them out when no numeral is used. Examples: 4 kg; enkele kilo.

options.label: Always abbreviate
options.rule: Always abbreviate units, whether or not a numeral is used. Examples: 4 kg; enkele kg.

options.label: Always spell out
options.rule: Always spell out units, whether or not a numeral is used. Examples: 4 kilo; enkele kilo.

options.label: Use a space between numeral and unit
options.rule: Use a space between a numeral and the unit. Example: 4 kg.

options.label: Do not use a space between numeral and unit
options.rule: Do not use a space between a numeral and the unit. Example: 4kg.

options.label: Use the unit symbol with a space
options.rule: Write temperatures with the unit symbol after the number and a space in between. Examples: 32 °C; 98 °F; 273 K.

options.label: Use the unit symbol without a space
options.rule: Write temperatures with the unit symbol directly after the number, without a space. Examples: 32°C; 98°F; 273K.

options.label: Write the unit in words
options.rule: Write temperatures with the unit in words. Examples: 32 graden Celsius; 98 graden Fahrenheit.

options.label: Use double curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use double curly quotation marks for quotations. Example: “Dat is goed nieuws”, zei ze.

options.label: Use single curly quotation marks
options.rule: Use single curly quotation marks for quotations. Example: ‘Dat is goed nieuws’, zei ze.

options.label: Use double straight quotation marks
options.rule: Use double straight quotation marks for quotations. Example: "Dat is goed nieuws", zei ze.

options.label: Use double quotation marks first and single quotation marks for nested quotes
options.rule: Use double quotation marks for primary quotations and single quotation marks for nested quotations. Example: “Hij zei: ‘Ik kom later.’”

options.label: Use single quotation marks first and double quotation marks for nested quotes
options.rule: Use single quotation marks for primary quotations and double quotation marks for nested quotations. Example: ‘Hij zei: “Ik kom later.”’

options.label: Use an en dash for ranges
options.rule: Use an en dash for ranges. Examples: maandag–vrijdag; 2001–2003.

options.label: Use a hyphen for ranges
options.rule: Use a hyphen for ranges. Examples: maandag-vrijdag; 2001-2003.

options.label: Use van ... tot
options.rule: Write ranges using “van ... tot”. Examples: van maandag tot vrijdag; van 2001 tot 2003.

options.label: Use curly apostrophes
options.rule: Use curly apostrophes. Examples: m’n; ’s avonds.

options.label: Use straight apostrophes
options.rule: Use straight apostrophes. Examples: m'n; 's avonds.

options.label: Use the ellipsis character
options.rule: Use the single ellipsis character. Example: Nog even wachten….

options.label: Use three periods
options.rule: Use three periods for an ellipsis. Example: Nog even wachten....

options.label: Use abbreviations sparingly
options.rule: Use abbreviations sparingly and prefer fully written words when clarity benefits. Example: bijvoorbeeld in plaats van bv..

options.label: Use common abbreviations
options.rule: Use common abbreviations where they are standard and unambiguous. Examples: bv.; m.a.w.; ca..

rules.title: Capitalization
rules.rule: Avoid writing entire words or sentences in capitals, except for acronyms, initialisms, and official names.

options.label: Prefer active voice
options.rule: Prefer active voice and use passive voice only when the agent is unknown, irrelevant, or intentionally omitted.

options.label: Allow passive voice where it improves focus
options.rule: Use passive voice where it improves focus on the action or result rather than the actor.

options.label: Prefer Dutch equivalents
examples: e-mailen in plaats van mailen wanneer formeel bedoeld
options.rule: Prefer established Dutch equivalents over English loanwords where a natural Dutch alternative exists. Examples: bijlage in plaats van attachment; gegevens in plaats van data when context permits.

options.label: Allow established English loanwords
options.rule: Use established English loanwords as they are when they are common and clear in Dutch usage. Examples: update; feedback; deadline.

options.label: Spell out low numbers
options.rule: Spell out low numbers in running text where this improves readability. Examples: twee deelnemers; negen dagen.

options.label: Prefer numerals
options.rule: Prefer numerals for most numbers, including low numbers, for consistency and scannability. Examples: 2 deelnemers; 9 dagen.

options.label: Use u
options.rule: Address the reader formally using “u”.

options.label: Use je
options.rule: Address the reader informally using “je”.

options.label: Prefer neutral words and job titles
options.rule: Prefer gender-neutral words and job titles where possible. Examples: voorzitter; medewerker; politieagent.

options.label: Use double forms for masculine and feminine references
options.rule: Use double forms where explicitly naming both masculine and feminine forms is preferred. Examples: medewerkers en medewerksters; lezers en lezeressen.

options.label: Use a direct and concise tone
options.rule: Use a direct, concise, and practical tone.

options.label: Use a warm and accessible tone
options.rule: Use a warm, friendly, and accessible tone.

options.label: Use a formal and neutral tone
options.rule: Use a formal, neutral, and precise tone.

rules.title: Anglicisms
rules.rule: Avoid unnecessary anglicisms when a natural and widely understood Dutch equivalent exists.
